questions.q: Why does Oracle Fusion Cloud Financials provide several different reporting tools instead of one tool for everything?
options: Because older tools were never retired
Financial reporting is really several different jobs — formatted statements, ad hoc exploration, pixel-perfect scheduled output, and Excel-native analysis — and no single tool is good at all of them
Because each tool requires a different login
Oracle requires customers to purchase at least four products
questions.explain: A tool built for fast ad hoc slicing is typically weak at pixel-perfect statutory output, so Oracle ships purpose-built tools for each distinct reporting job.

questions.q: Which tool is purpose-built for formatted financial statements like the Income Statement and Balance Sheet?
options: BI Publisher
Smart View Report Packages
Financial Reporting Studio
OTBI dashboards
questions.explain: Financial Reporting Studio (Financial Reporting Web Studio) builds grid-based formatted statements run against GL balances, with a defined point of view.

questions.q: A collections analyst wants to slice open receivables by customer and age bucket right now, without waiting on IT. Which tool best fits that need?
options: OTBI, for ad hoc real-time exploration
BI Publisher, for pixel-perfect scheduled output
Financial Reporting Studio, for formatted statements
None of these tools support that kind of analysis
questions.explain: OTBI is designed for drag-and-drop, real-time ad hoc analysis over curated subject areas, exactly this kind of same-day exploration.

questions.q: Where does the Financial Reporting Center live inside Oracle Fusion Cloud Financials?
options: It is a separate application requiring its own login
Inside the General Accounting work area
Only inside Microsoft Excel
Inside the Scheduled Processes work area
questions.explain: The Financial Reporting Center is a page inside the General Accounting work area, not a standalone application.

questions.q: Which tool is a Microsoft Office add-in that connects live to a Fusion environment for spreadsheet-based analysis?
options: BI Publisher
Financial Reporting Studio
OTBI
Smart View
questions.explain: Smart View installs as an Excel/Office add-in and connects out to Fusion, giving a familiar spreadsheet interface for pivoting live ledger balances.
